newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's EDF wants to step up foreign investments.
newsitem.headline: France's EDF wants to step up foreign investments.

text.p: Electricite de France, the state electricity utility, could invest up to 16 billion francs abroad over four years, its chairman Edmond Alphandery said.
In an interview due to be released on Wednesday by Les Echos newspaper, Alphandery said the French state had authorised the company to invest 13 billion francs abroad under its new contract plan.
But adding cash flow and funds used to finance foreign investments, that amount could reach 16 billion francs, Alphandery said.
"I even target a total of 16 bilion francs over four years," he said.
Electricite de France invested some seven billion francs abroad under its previous contract for 1993-1996.
Alphandery also said Electricite de France would continue to invest one billion francs in France each year.
He said the new contract plan included plans to cut electricity prices by 15 percent between 1997 and the year 2000.
